extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts that focuses on visual and logical reasoning. It includes 9.6K human-written questions and 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries over 20,882 real-world charts.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four online sources, with chart images collected from Pew and chart images plus underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and text descriptions extracted from the other three sources. Human-authored QA pairs were then collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk, and additional QA pairs were automatically generated from human-written chart summaries using a fine-tuned T5 model, with manual validation and filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Invalid machine-generated questions were filtered out using a heuristic that removed questions whose answers could not be found in the chart data table, and the machine-generated test set was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data consisted of real-world charts from Statista, Pew Research, Our World in Data, and OECD, including chart images; for three sources also underlying data tables, metadata such as title and chart type, SVG files, associated text descriptions, and bounding box information for chart elements extracted from SVG files.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA pairs were collected via an Amazon Mechanical Turk task where crowdworkers were instructed to write two types of questions per chart—compositional questions involving at least two mathematical/logical operations and visual questions referring to visual attributes such as color, height, and length—and provide answers. Each chart received two questions from one worker, and the same questions were answered by another annotator; exact-match agreement was used for validation, with manual adjudication when answers differed. Additionally, machine-generated QA pairs were produced from human-written chart summaries using fine-tuned T5 models, then filtered heuristically and partially manually validated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was analyzed using inter-annotator agreement based on exact match and manual review. Exact-match agreement between crowdworkers was 61.04%, and a manual check of 500 random samples found agreement increased to 78.55% when accounting for typos and lexical variations. For machine-generated questions, a heuristic filter removed invalid questions, and manual analysis of 1,250 QA pairs found 86.64% were complete, answerable, and correct.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For human-authored annotation, each chart received two questions from one worker, and each of those questions was answered by one additional annotator.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Fine-tuned T5 models were used for machine generation of QA pairs: one model for answer extraction and another for answer-aware question generation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may reflect topical and source biases from the four crawled online sources, with some topics overrepresented such as U.S. politics and policy in the Pew subset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include invalid machine-generated questions due to domain mismatch, reliance on heuristics to filter them, remaining quality issues despite filtering, OCR/data extraction errors, and challenges from linguistic variation, typos, and lexical variation. The paper also notes that gold data tables are often unavailable in real-world settings.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes charts and questions covering demographic and social attributes such as gender, age groups, geography, language variation, and public opinion/political topics.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for Chart Question Answering, supporting training, validation, and testing of models for answering questions about charts with visual and logical reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The code and dataset are publicly available.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Crawled charts from four sources; for Pew only chart images were collected because tables were unavailable; for the other sources, underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and text descriptions were extracted; bounding box information for chart elements was extracted from SVG files to train data extraction models.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: “The Pew research (pewresearch.org) publishes report about social and economic issues, demographic trends and public opinion with a wide variety of charts.”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: “We present a large-scale benchmark covering 9,608 human-written questions as well as 23,111 questions generated from human-written chart summaries.”

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: “Our code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/vis-nlp/ChartQA”

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “we crawled charts from four different sources... For the Pew dataset, we only crawled chart images since the underlying data tables are not available.
